chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Matar ibn Arqam, who said:

I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام say: “Indeed, Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar, the governor, sent for me, so I went to him, and before him were two men. One of them had assaulted his companion and scratched his face. He said: ‘What do you say, O Aba Abdillah, regarding these two men?’ I said: ‘And what did they say?’ He said: ‘One of them said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله has superiority over Banu Umayyah in lineage-nobility. The other said: He has superiority over all people in every good thing. The one who supported the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله became angry and did to his face what you see. So is anything due upon him?’”

So I said to him: ‘I think that you have already asked those around you and they informed you.’ He said: ‘I adjure you that you must speak.’ So I said to him: ‘The one who claimed that anyone is like the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in excellence ought to have been killed and not spared.’”

He said: “Then he said: ‘Is not nobility one?’ So I said: ‘Indeed, hasab is not nasab. Do you not see that if you stayed with a man from some of these Abyssinians and he hosted you, then you said of him: This man is noble?’ He said: ‘Is not lineage one?’ I said: ‘When they both meet at Adam, then lineage is one. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was not mixed with shirk nor with transgression, so he ordered concerning him, and he was killed.’”

key_terms.الْحَسَبُ: social nobility or honorable standing distinct from lineage
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: superiority or excellence in rank and virtue
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rule about someone who equates others with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in excellence?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a case brought before Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام concerning two men disputing over the superiority of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. The Imam states a severe legal judgment against the one who equated anyone with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله in excellence, and he distinguishes between inherited lineage and acquired nobility.
